question: Which of the following morphological features do we expect to find in the biopsy of the gastric body of a patient with vitamin B12 deficiency?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Vitamin B12 deficiency" -> "pernicious anemia" -> "autoimmune gastritis" -> "gastric mucosal atrophy" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Vitamin B12 deficiency" -> "chronic gastritis" -> "possible Helicobacter pylori infection" -> 50%
CHAIN: "Vitamin B12 deficiency" -> "chronic gastritis" -> "endocrine cell hyperplasia" -> 60%
analysis: Vitamin B12 deficiency is often associated with pernicious anemia, which is characterized by atrophic gastritis. In the gastric body, this condition leads to the loss of gastric glandular cells, resulting in atrophy. This is due to the autoimmune destruction of parietal cells, which are responsible for producing intrinsic factor necessary for vitamin B12 absorption.
